skills.title: Recognise and extend the odd and even number sequences
Recognise and extend triangular and square number sequences
Recognise cube numbers and powers, and state a sequence's rule in words

expectations: A sequence is a list of numbers made by a rule, and the rule has to work for every term, not only the first two or three
Odd numbers start at 1 and go up by 2; even numbers start at 2 and go up by 2
Triangular numbers add 1, then 2, then 3, then 4 … (1, 3, 6, 10, 15); square numbers are n × n (1, 4, 9, 16, 25)
Cube numbers are n × n × n (1, 8, 27, 64, 125); powers of 2 double each time (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
Saying the rule in words lets you find any term, such as the 10th, without listing all the ones before it

misconceptions.belief: Believes a sequence is fixed by its first two terms, so 1, 3, … must continue 5, 7
signs: Continues 1, 3, 6 with 8 or 9 because it 'started with +2'
Says only one sequence can begin 1, 4
Never looks at the third term before deciding the rule

diagnostic.prompt_en: Ravi says: 'The sequence starts 1, 4, so the next number has to be 7.' Is he right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ravi kehta hai: 'Sequence 1, 4 se shuru hota hai, toh agla number 7 hi hoga.' Kya woh sahi hai?

options.text: Not necessarily: 1, 4, 7 (add 3) and 1, 4, 9 (squares) both start with 1, 4
Yes, after 1, 4 the next number is always 7
Yes, because every sequence adds the same amount each time

remediation.representation: Two sequences written one above the other that share the first two terms and then split apart
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts the third term of both, then the tutor reveals they differ; ask what extra information we needed to know the rule

misconceptions.belief: Thinks every sequence grows by adding the same number each time
signs: Continues 1, 4, 9 with 14 (adds 5 again)
Continues triangular numbers 1, 3, 6 with 9
Looks at only the last gap to find the next term

diagnostic.prompt_en: What comes next: 1, 4, 9, 16, …?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Agla number kya aayega: 1, 4, 9, 16, …?

options.text: 23, because the last jump was 7
32, because you double

remediation.representation: A difference ladder: write the sequence and the gaps underneath (3, 5, 7, …), alongside growing dot squares
remediation.moveShape: Child writes the gaps themselves and spots that the gaps change; ask what the next gap must be before computing the term

misconceptions.belief: Confuses squaring with doubling (and cubing with tripling)
signs: Says 5 squared is 10
Says 3 cubed is 9
Writes the square numbers as 2, 4, 6, 8

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is the 6th square number?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 6th square number kya hai?

remediation.representation: A 6 by 6 tile grid next to a row of 6 + 6 tiles
remediation.moveShape: Child builds both from tiles and counts; ask which picture is 'six sixes' and which is 'two sixes'

items.prompt_en: What are the next two odd numbers after 11?
items.prompt_hi: 11 ke baad agle do odd numbers kaun se hain?
items.answer: 13 and 15
hints: Odd numbers jump by how much?
Odd numbers go up by 2 each time.
13 and 15, each 2 more than the one before.

items.prompt_en: Triangular numbers go 1, 3, 6, 10, … What are the next two?
items.prompt_hi: Triangular numbers aise chalte hain: 1, 3, 6, 10, … Agle do kaun se honge?
items.answer: 15 and 21
hints: How much did we add each time so far?
We added 2, then 3, then 4; the jump grows by 1.
15 and 21: add 5, then add 6.

items.prompt_en: Squares: 1, 4, 9, 16. Before you work it out, predict: will the jump from 16 to the next square be bigger or smaller than 7?
items.prompt_hi: Squares: 1, 4, 9, 16. Calculate karne se pehle guess karo: 16 se agle square tak ki jump 7 se badi hogi ya chhoti?
items.answer: Bigger: the next square is 25, a jump of 9
hints: What were the jumps so far?
The jumps were 3, 5, 7; what kind of numbers are those?
The jumps are odd numbers, so the next jump is ___.
Bigger: the jump is 9, so the next square is 25.

items.prompt_en: You found the next square after 16 is 25. Why do the jumps between squares keep growing?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne nikala 16 ke baad agla square 25 hai. Squares ke beech ki jump badhti kyon jaati hai?
items.answer: To grow an n by n square into the next one you add a row and a column around it, and each new border is 2 longer than the last, so the jumps are the odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9 …
acceptable: add a row and a column
hints: Picture a 4 by 4 square of dots. What must you add to make 5 by 5?
You add a new row and a new column, sharing a corner.
From 4 by 4 to 5 by 5 you add 4 + 4 + 1 = ___ dots.
Each step adds a border that is 2 bigger than before, so the jumps are 3, 5, 7, 9: the odd numbers.

verified.solverAnswer: jumps are consecutive odd numbers; each L-shaped border is 2 more than the last

items.prompt_en: What are the first four cube numbers?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle chaar cube numbers kaun se hain?
hints: What does 'cube' mean: how many times do you multiply the number?
A cube number is n × n × n.

items.prompt_en: Look at 1, 3, 5, 7 and at 1, 3, 6, 10. Both start 1, 3. What is different about their rules?
items.prompt_hi: 1, 3, 5, 7 aur 1, 3, 6, 10 dekho. Dono 1, 3 se shuru hote hain. Dono ke rule mein kya fark hai?
items.answer: The first adds 2 every time (odd numbers); the second adds 2, then 3, then 4 (triangular numbers)
acceptable: first adds 2 each time, second adds one more each time
hints: Write the jumps under each sequence.
One has jumps 2, 2, 2; the other has 2, 3, 4.
First rule: add ___ every time. Second rule: add 2, 3, 4, ___.
Same start, different rules: the odd numbers add 2 every time, the triangular numbers add 1 more each time.

verified.solverAnswer: 1,3,5,7 adds constant 2 (odd numbers); 1,3,6,10 adds a growing jump 2,3,4

items.prompt_en: A shop stacks small cube-shaped boxes into bigger cubes: 1 box, then 2 by 2 by 2, then 3 by 3 by 3. How many small boxes make the 5 by 5 by 5 cube?
items.prompt_hi: Ek dukaan chhote cube jaise dabbon ko bade cubes mein lagati hai: 1 dabba, phir 2 by 2 by 2, phir 3 by 3 by 3. 5 by 5 by 5 wale cube mein kitne chhote dabbe lagenge?
hints: How many boxes are in one layer of the 5 by 5 by 5 cube?
One layer is 5 by 5 = 25 boxes. How many layers?
25 boxes per layer × 5 layers = ___.

items.prompt_en: My friend wrote the square numbers as 1, 4, 9, 16, 23. Find the mistake.
items.prompt_hi: Mere dost ne square numbers aise likhe: 1, 4, 9, 16, 23. Galti dhoondo.
items.answer: 23 is wrong; the next square is 5 × 5 = 25 (the jump should be 9, not 7)
hints: Check the last number: is 23 something times itself?
After 4 × 4 = 16 comes 5 × 5.
5 × 5 = ___, so the jump from 16 is ___.
23 is wrong; it should be 25. He repeated the jump of 7 instead of using 9.

items.prompt_en: Describe how you would draw the 4th triangular number with dots. How many dots are there?
items.prompt_hi: Batao, 4th triangular number ko dots se kaise banaoge? Kitne dots honge?
items.answer: Rows of 1, 2, 3 and 4 dots stacked into a triangle: 10 dots
hints: What does the first triangular number look like?
Each new triangle gets a new bottom row with one more dot.
Stack rows of 1, 2, 3 and 4 dots: 10 dots in a triangle.

items.prompt_en: At a mela stall, glasses are stacked in a triangle: 1 on top, 2 below it, 3 below that, and so on. The bottom row has 8 glasses. How many glasses in all?
items.prompt_hi: Mele ki ek stall pe glasses triangle mein rakhe hain: upar 1, uske neeche 2, phir 3, aise hi. Sabse neeche wali row mein 8 glasses hain. Kul kitne glasses hain?
hints: Which sequence does this stack make?
It is a triangular number: 1 + 2 + … + 8.
36 glasses, the 8th triangular number.

items.prompt_en: Teach your cousin the difference between square numbers and cube numbers using the number 3.
items.prompt_hi: Apne cousin ko 3 ka example lekar samjhao ki square number aur cube number mein kya fark hai.
items.answer: 3 squared is 3 × 3 = 9, a flat 3 by 3 square; 3 cubed is 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, a 3 by 3 by 3 block of 3 layers
hints: How would you build '3 squared' with tiles?
A square is flat; a cube has layers too.
3 × 3 = ___ for the square, and 3 × 3 × 3 = ___ for the cube.
Square: 3 × 3 = 9 in a flat square. Cube: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, three layers of 9.

items.prompt_en: Quick! What is the 10th even number?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! 10th even number kaunsa hai?
hints: Even numbers are 2, 4, 6 …
The nth even number is 2 × n.

items.prompt_en: Powers of 2 go 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. What comes next, and what is the rule?
items.prompt_hi: Powers of 2 aise chalte hain: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Agla kya aayega, aur rule kya hai?
items.answer: 32; each term is double the one before
hints: Compare each number with the one before it.
Is it adding the same amount, or multiplying?
32: the rule is 'double the last one'.

items.prompt_en: A triangular arrangement of seats grows by adding a new row each time. Its totals are 6, 10, 15, … How many seats are in the next arrangement?
items.prompt_hi: Seats ki triangular arrangement mein har baar ek nayi row judti hai. Totals 6, 10, 15, … hain. Agli arrangement mein kitni seats hongi?
items.answer: 21 seats
hints: How many seats were added between the last two arrangements?
Each new row has one more seat than the previous new row.
The next total is 15 + ___.
21 seats; the new row adds 6.

items.prompt_en: A triangular display has 28 lights in seven rows: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7. If the organisers add two more rows, how many lights will it have?
items.prompt_hi: Ek triangular display ki saat rows mein 28 lights hain: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7. Organisers do aur rows jod dein, toh total kitni lights hongi?
items.answer: 45 lights
hints: How many lights go in each of the two new rows?
Continue the row sizes after the seventh row.
New total = 28 + ___ + ___.
45 lights; rows of 8 and 9 are added.

items.prompt_en: A game awards points in this sequence: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125. What rule gives the points for level n?
items.prompt_hi: Ek game mein points ka sequence hai: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125. Level n ke points nikaalne ka rule kya hai?
items.answer: Cube n (n × n × n)
acceptable: multiply n by itself three times
hints: Could each term depend on its level number?
Compare a term with repeated multiplication of its level number.
Points at level n = n × ___ × ___.
Cube n: multiply the level number by itself three times.

workedExample.problem: Find the 7th triangular number and say the rule in words.
steps: Triangular numbers start at 1 and add 2, then 3, then 4, and so on.
1, 3, 6, 10, 15 are the first five.
Rule in words: the nth triangular number is 1 + 2 + … + n.
fadedVersion: Triangular numbers start at 1 and add 2, then ___, then 4, and so on.
1, 3, 6, 10, ___ are the first five.
Rule in words: the nth triangular number is 1 + 2 + … + ___.

skills.title: Draw dot pictures for square and triangular numbers
Use a picture to show how a sequence grows from one term to the next
Use a picture as an argument for why a pattern is true

expectations: A square number can be drawn as a square of dots: n rows of n dots
A triangular number can be drawn as a triangle: rows of 1, 2, 3, … dots
Growing a square by one step adds an L-shaped border: a new row and a new column that share a corner, so 4 by 4 to 5 by 5 adds 4 + 4 + 1 = 9
Two copies of a triangle fit together into a rectangle n by (n + 1), so a triangular number is half of that rectangle
A picture can show WHY a pattern holds at every step, not only that it worked once

misconceptions.belief: Thinks pictures are decoration and cannot prove anything in maths
signs: Says 'the picture is just drawing, the real answer is the number'
Cannot use a drawing to explain where a number came from
Skips the picture and recounts every time

diagnostic.prompt_en: Meena draws 4 by 4 dots, then adds an L-shape of 9 dots to get 5 by 5. What does her picture tell us?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Meena 4 by 4 dots banati hai, phir 9 dots ka L-shape jodkar 5 by 5 bana deti hai. Uski picture humein kya batati hai?

options.text: That 16 + 9 = 25, and why the jump from one square to the next is an odd number
Nothing, a picture is only a drawing
That 16 + 8 = 24, since the L is 4 dots one way and 4 the other

remediation.representation: Coins or dots that the child physically extends from one square to the next, with each new border coloured differently
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to predict the next border size from the picture alone, then check by counting; name that the picture predicted it

misconceptions.belief: When growing a square by one step, counts the shared corner twice or forgets it (4 by 4 to 5 by 5 adds 8 or 10 dots)
signs: Says 6 by 6 to 7 by 7 adds 14
Says it adds 6 + 6 = 12
Adds a row and a column of the old length and forgets the corner

diagnostic.prompt_en: To grow a 4 by 4 square of dots into a 5 by 5 square, how many new dots do you need?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 4 by 4 dots ke square ko 5 by 5 banane ke liye kitne naye dots chahiye?

remediation.representation: An L-shaped border in a second colour placed around the old square on a dot grid
remediation.moveShape: Child counts the new row, then the new column, and the tutor points to the corner dot; ask whether it belongs to the row, the column, or both

misconceptions.belief: Thinks any arrangement of dots in rows shows a square number (e.g., 3 rows of 4 'is a square')
signs: Calls 12 a square number because it makes 3 rows of 4
Draws 9 dots in a straight line as a 'square'
Does not check that rows and columns are equal

diagnostic.prompt_en: 12 dots can be arranged as 3 rows of 4. Is 12 a square number?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 12 dots ko 3 rows mein 4-4 karke laga sakte hain. Kya 12 square number hai?

options.text: No, 3 rows of 4 is a rectangle; a square needs equal rows and columns
Yes, any rows of dots make a square
Yes, because the dots are in neat rows

remediation.representation: Side-by-side dot arrays 3 by 3, 3 by 4 and 4 by 4 with their sides measured
remediation.moveShape: Child sorts arrays into 'square' and 'not square' and states the test they used; ask for the nearest square to 12 on each side

items.prompt_en: How many dots are there in a square picture with 6 rows of 6 dots?
items.prompt_hi: Ek square picture mein 6 rows hain aur har row mein 6 dots. Kul kitne dots hain?
hints: How many dots in one row?
6 rows, each with 6 dots.
36 dots.

items.prompt_en: Describe the dot picture of the 5th triangular number. How many dots in each row and in total?
items.prompt_hi: 5th triangular number ki dot picture batao. Har row mein kitne dots hain aur total kitne?
items.answer: Rows of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 dots: 15 dots in total
hints: What does the top row have?
Each row has one more dot than the row above it.
Rows of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5: 15 dots.

items.prompt_en: You have coins in a 6 by 6 square. Guess before you count: how many more coins make it 7 by 7?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare paas 6 by 6 square mein coins hain. Ginne se pehle guess karo: 7 by 7 banane ke liye aur kitne coins chahiye?
hints: What has to be added along one side and along the top?
A new row of 6, a new column of 6, and one corner coin.

items.prompt_en: Why does the L-shape that turns 6 by 6 into 7 by 7 have 13 dots and not 14?
items.prompt_hi: 6 by 6 ko 7 by 7 banane wale L-shape mein 13 dots kyon hain, 14 kyon nahi?
items.answer: The new row has 7 dots and the new column has 7 dots, but they share the corner dot, so 7 + 7 − 1 = 13
hints: Point to the corner dot of the L-shape. Is it in the row or the column?
It is in both, so it must not be counted twice.
The corner is shared, so 7 + 7 − 1 = 13 dots.

verified.solverAnswer: 7 on one side + 6 on the other; corner dot shared, so 13 not 14

items.prompt_en: One picture has 12 dots as 3 rows of 4. Another has 9 dots as 3 rows of 3. Which shows a square number, and how can you tell?
items.prompt_hi: Ek picture mein 12 dots 3 rows mein 4-4 hain. Doosri mein 9 dots 3 rows mein 3-3. Kaunsi square number dikhati hai, aur kaise pata?
items.answer: The 9-dot picture: rows and columns are equal (3 by 3); 3 by 4 is a rectangle
hints: Count the rows and the dots in each row for both.
A square needs the same number both ways.
3 rows of ___ is square; 3 rows of 4 is a ___.
9 is the square number: 3 by 3. 12 as 3 by 4 is a rectangle.

verified.solverAnswer: 3 rows of 3 (9) is square: rows = columns

items.prompt_en: Two triangles of 10 dots each (rows of 1 to 4) are fitted together, one turned upside down. What shape do they make, and how many dots?
items.prompt_hi: 10-10 dots ke do triangle (rows 1 se 4) ko jodte hain, ek ko ulta karke. Kaunsa shape banta hai aur kitne dots?
items.answer: A 4 by 5 rectangle with 20 dots, so the triangle is half of it
hints: Each row of the first triangle sits next to a row of the second. How long does each joined row become?
Rows of 1 and 4, 2 and 3, 3 and 2, 4 and 1 each make 5.
4 rows of 5 = ___ dots.
A 4 by 5 rectangle of 20 dots; each triangle is half, 10.

items.prompt_en: A rangoli triangle with rows of 1, 2, 3, … dots has 21 dots. How many dots go in the next new bottom row, and what is the new total?
items.prompt_hi: Ek rangoli triangle mein rows 1, 2, 3, … dots ki hain aur kul 21 dots hain. Agli nayi bottom row mein kitne dots honge, aur naya total kya hoga?
items.answer: 7 dots in the new row; 28 in total
hints: How many rows make 21 dots?
1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 21, so there are 6 rows.
The next row has ___ dots, so 21 + 7 = ___.
The new row has 7 dots, making 28.

items.prompt_en: My claim: to grow a 9 by 9 dot square into 10 by 10, you add 20 dots. Check it.
items.prompt_hi: Mera claim: 9 by 9 dots ke square ko 10 by 10 banane ke liye 20 dots jodne padenge. Check karo.
items.answer: Wrong: you add 19 dots (10 + 9, or 100 − 81)
hints: Work out 10 × 10 and 9 × 9.
The new dots are the difference between the two squares.
19, not 20: the corner dot was counted twice.

items.prompt_en: A courtyard is tiled as an 8 by 8 square. The owner wants a 9 by 9 square. New tiles cost ₹20 each. How much will the extra tiles cost?
items.prompt_hi: Ek aangan 8 by 8 square tiles se bana hai. Maalik 9 by 9 square chahta hai. Har nayi tile ₹20 ki hai. Extra tiles kitne ki padengi?
items.answer: ₹340 (17 new tiles × ₹20)
hints: How many tiles are in the border that makes 8 by 8 into 9 by 9?
17 new tiles, so ₹340.

items.prompt_en: Riya says, 'Pictures are just for fun, real maths is only numbers.' Using the two-triangles-make-a-rectangle picture, how would you show her a picture can tell us something true?
items.prompt_hi: Riya kehti hai, 'Pictures bas mazze ke liye hain, asli maths sirf numbers hai.' Do-triangle-milke-rectangle wali picture se usse kaise dikhaoge ki picture bhi sach batati hai?
items.answer: The picture shows any triangular number is half of an n by (n + 1) rectangle, e.g. 10 = (4 × 5) ÷ 2, and it works for every size because two copies always fit that way
hints: What shape do two equal triangles of dots make?
They make a rectangle one longer than it is tall.
So triangle = half of rows × (rows + 1): for 4 rows, half of 4 × 5 = ___.
Two triangles always make an n by n+1 rectangle, so every triangular number is half of it; the picture proves it for all sizes.

verified.solverAnswer: two 1-4 triangles fit into 4x5 rectangle of 20 dots so triangle = 10; a picture shows a true fact

items.prompt_en: Teach a younger friend how to draw the next square from a picture of 4 by 4 dots.
items.prompt_hi: Apne chhote dost ko sikhao ki 4 by 4 dots ki picture se agla square kaise banate hain.
items.answer: Add a new row of 4 along the bottom, a new column of 4 along the side, and 1 corner dot: 9 new dots, giving 5 by 5 = 25
acceptable: add row and column and corner
hints: Where will the new dots go?
One new row, one new column, and the corner where they meet.
4 + 4 + 1 = ___ new dots, total ___.
Add an L-shape: 4 + 4 + 1 = 9 dots, making a 5 by 5 square of 25.

verified.solverAnswer: add L-shaped border of 9 dots (4+4+1) to make 5x5=25

items.prompt_en: Quick! Triangle dots go 1, 3, 6. What is the next triangular number?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi! Triangle dots 1, 3, 6. Agla triangular number?
hints: How many dots in the next row?
The new bottom row has 4 dots.

items.prompt_en: A game screen shows dots in a 3-by-3 square. You add one new row and one new column to make a 4-by-4 square. How many new dots are needed?
items.prompt_hi: Game screen par dots ka 3-by-3 square hai. Use 4-by-4 square banane ke liye ek nayi row aur ek naya column jodte ho. Kitne naye dots chahiye?
items.answer: 7 dots
hints: Where would you draw the new row and column?
Count their dots, but watch where they meet.
New dots = row + column − shared dot = ___.
7 dots; the new row and column share one corner dot.

items.prompt_en: A phone game shows a 12-by-12 square of dots. To grow it into a 13-by-13 square, a player adds a row and a column. How many dots are added?
items.prompt_hi: Phone game mein dots ka 12-by-12 square hai. Use 13-by-13 banane ke liye ek row aur ek column jodte hain. Kitne dots judenge?
items.answer: 25 dots
hints: Will the new row and column have a dot in common?
Count both new edges, then correct for their shared corner.
Dots added = new row + new column − shared corner = ___.
25 dots; two edges of 13 share one corner.

items.prompt_en: To grow an 8-by-8 tile square into a 9-by-9 square, Arjun draws a new row of 9 and a new column of 9. Why does adding 9 + 9 give one tile too many?
items.prompt_hi: 8-by-8 tiles ka square 9-by-9 banane ke liye Arjun 9 tiles ki nayi row aur 9 tiles ka naya column banata hai. 9 + 9 ginne par ek tile zyada kyun aata hai?
items.answer: The new row and column share a corner tile, which gets counted twice.
acceptable: One tile belongs to both the row and column
common corner ko do baar gina
hints: Do the new row and new column touch?
Look at the corner where the two new edges meet.
The tile at their meeting point is counted ___.
Their shared corner tile is counted twice, so subtract one.

verified.solverAnswer: The corner tile is counted twice.
verified.note: Both identify double-counted corner tile

workedExample.problem: Use a picture to find how many dots turn a 5 by 5 square into a 6 by 6 square.
steps: Draw the 5 by 5 square: 25 dots.
Add a new row of 5 dots along the bottom.
Add a new column of 5 dots along the right side.
Add 1 corner dot where the new row and column meet.
fadedVersion: Draw the 5 by 5 square: ___ dots.
Add a new row of ___ dots along the bottom.
Add a new column of 5 dots along the right side.
Add ___ corner dot where the new row and column meet.

skills.title: Show that adding consecutive odd numbers from 1 gives square numbers
Show that two consecutive triangular numbers add to a square number
Test a pattern on new cases and explain with a picture why it always works

expectations: 1 + 3 + 5 + … (the first n odd numbers, starting at 1) = n × n, because each odd number is the next L-shaped border around the square
Adding counting numbers up and then down, like 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1, gives a square number (here 16)
Two triangular numbers next to each other, like 6 and 10, fit together into a square (16)
The sum must start at 1 and use consecutive odd numbers; skipping or starting later breaks it
Checking a few cases is not proof; a picture that works for every step shows why the pattern is always true

misconceptions.belief: Assumes a pattern seen in three cases is true for all cases without any reason
signs: Says 'it worked three times, so it always works'
Cannot give a reason or picture for a pattern
Surprised when a pattern breaks at the 6th case

diagnostic.prompt_en: Asha checks 1 + 3 = 4, 1 + 3 + 5 = 9, 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16 and says, 'So it works for all odd numbers.' What is the best next step?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Asha check karti hai: 1 + 3 = 4, 1 + 3 + 5 = 9, 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16, aur kehti hai, 'Toh yeh sab odd numbers ke liye chalega.' Sabse achha agla kadam kya hai?

options.text: Explain why, e.g. with a picture where each odd number is the next L-shape around a square
Nothing, three examples prove it
It is wrong, because 16 is not odd

remediation.representation: The circle-cutting pattern (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 pieces, then 31) shown next to the L-shape picture
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts the 6-point circle count, sees 31, and then compares with the L-shape picture that cannot break; ask what the picture gives that the examples did not

misconceptions.belief: Thinks adding odd numbers always gives an odd number
signs: Expects 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 to be odd
Rejects 16 as an answer because 'odd + odd should be odd'
Says 3 + 5 is odd

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is 3 + 5 odd or even?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 3 + 5 odd hai ya even?

options.text: Even, it is 8
Odd, because both numbers are odd

remediation.representation: Odd numbers as pairs of counters with one left over
remediation.moveShape: Child joins two 'odd' piles and sees the two leftovers pair up; ask what happens with three odd piles

misconceptions.belief: Thinks any run of odd numbers adds to a square, even if it does not start at 1 or skips one
signs: Claims 3 + 5 + 7 = 15 is a square
Adds 1 + 3 + 7 and expects a square
Does not notice the missing L-shapes

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which of these adds up to a square number?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Inme se kiska total square number hai?

remediation.representation: The L-shape square picture with one border removed (the 1 in the corner, or a middle border)
remediation.moveShape: Child tries to build the square with a missing piece and sees the gap; ask which odd number is needed to fill it

items.prompt_hi: 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 kitna hota hai?
hints: Add them in pairs from the ends.
25, which is 5 × 5.

items.prompt_en: Before adding, predict: what will 1 + 3 + 5 + … + 19 (the first 10 odd numbers) come to?
items.prompt_hi: Jodne se pehle guess karo: 1 + 3 + 5 + … + 19 (pehle 10 odd numbers) ka total kya hoga?
hints: What did the first 5 odd numbers add up to?
The first n odd numbers make n × n.
10 odd numbers make 10 × 10 = ___.

items.prompt_en: You said the first 10 odd numbers add to 100. Why does that make 10 × 10?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha pehle 10 odd numbers ka total 100 hai. Yeh 10 × 10 kyon banta hai?
items.answer: Each odd number is an L-shaped border that turns a k by k square into a (k+1) by (k+1) square; after 10 borders, starting from 1, you have a 10 by 10 square
acceptable: each odd number grows the square
hints: Picture 1 dot, then add 3 around it. What shape do you get?
Each next odd number wraps around the square as an L.
After 10 L-shapes the square is ___ by ___.
Each odd number is the next L-shaped border, so 10 of them build a 10 by 10 square of 100 dots.

verified.solverAnswer: each odd number is an L-border added to square; 10 odd numbers build a 10 by 10 square

items.prompt_en: Add the 3rd and 4th triangular numbers, 6 and 10. What kind of number do you get?
items.prompt_hi: 3rd aur 4th triangular numbers, 6 aur 10, ko jodo. Kis tarah ka number milta hai?
items.answer: 16, a square number (4 × 4)
hints: What is 6 + 10?
Is 16 in any sequence you know?
16, a square number: 4 × 4.

items.prompt_en: Describe a dot picture that shows 10 + 15 = 25 using two triangles.
items.prompt_hi: Do triangles se ek dot picture batao jo dikhaye ki 10 + 15 = 25.
items.answer: A triangle with rows 1 to 4 (10 dots) and a triangle with rows 1 to 5 (15 dots) fit together along a diagonal into a 5 by 5 square
acceptable: two triangles make a 5 by 5 square
hints: How many rows does the 15-dot triangle have?
Turn the smaller triangle and slide it against the bigger one.
Rows of 5 + 0, 4 + 1, 3 + 2 … each make ___, giving a ___ by 5 square.
The 15-triangle and the 10-triangle fit together into a 5 by 5 square of 25 dots.

verified.solverAnswer: triangle of 4 rows (10) and triangle of 5 rows (15) fit to make 5x5 square of 25

items.prompt_en: Up and down: what is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1? What kind of number is it?
items.prompt_hi: Upar aur neeche: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 kitna hai? Yeh kis tarah ka number hai?
items.answer: 25, a square number (5 × 5)
hints: Pair up the numbers on either side of the 5.
1 + 4, 2 + 3 … or look for a square.
15 going up + 10 coming down = ___.
25, a square number: going up to n and back down gives n × n.

items.prompt_en: My working: 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25, a square, because odd numbers add to squares. Spot the mistake.
items.prompt_hi: Meri working: 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25, ek square, kyunki odd numbers jodne se square banta hai. Galti dhoondo.
items.answer: 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 is 24, not 25, and it is not a square; the sum must start at 1
hints: Add 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 again carefully.
Which odd number is missing from the start?
3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = ___; we need to add ___ to make a square.
It is 24, not a square: the 1 in the corner is missing. 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25.

verified.solverAnswer: 3+5+7+9=24 not 25; sum of odds starting at 1 only gives squares

items.prompt_en: Mark points on a circle and join every pair. 2 points cut it into 2 pieces, 3 points into 4, 4 points into 8, 5 points into 16. Predict the number of pieces for 6 points.
items.prompt_hi: Circle pe points lagao aur har pair ko line se jodo. 2 points se 2 tukde, 3 se 4, 4 se 8, 5 se 16. 6 points ke liye kitne tukde guess karoge?
items.answer: 31 at most, not 32: the doubling pattern breaks
hints: What pattern do 2, 4, 8, 16 suggest?
Everyone guesses doubling, but count carefully when you draw it.
Doubling says 32, but careful drawing gives ___.
31, not 32: a pattern that held four times still broke, so we need reasons, not just examples.

items.prompt_en: At a wedding, chairs are set in rows: 1 chair in the front row, 3 in the next, 5 in the next, and so on. With 12 rows, how many chairs are there?
items.prompt_hi: Ek shaadi mein kursiyan rows mein lagi hain: aage ki row mein 1, uske peeche 3, phir 5, aise hi. 12 rows hon toh kul kitni kursiyan?
hints: What kind of numbers are 1, 3, 5, …?
The first 12 odd numbers add up to a square.
144 chairs.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend why checking three examples is not enough to be sure a pattern is always true, and what you can do instead.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki teen examples check karna kaafi kyon nahi hai yeh pakka karne ke liye ki pattern hamesha sahi hai, aur iski jagah kya kar sakte hain.
items.answer: Examples can fit a pattern that later breaks (circle pieces 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, then 31); a picture or reason that works for every step, like the L-shapes, shows it is always true
hints: Can you think of a pattern that broke?
The circle pieces doubled four times and then did not.
Examples show it worked; a ___ shows why it always works.
Examples can mislead, as the circle 31 shows; a picture or argument that works at every step makes it certain.

verified.solverAnswer: pattern may break (6 points gives 31 not 32); need reasoning/proof/picture

items.prompt_en: Quick! What is the sum of the first 7 odd numbers?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi! Pehle 7 odd numbers ka total?
hints: The first n odd numbers make what?
They make n × n.

items.prompt_en: Why do two triangular numbers that are next to each other always make a square?
items.prompt_hi: Do lagataar triangular numbers milkar hamesha square kyon banate hain?
items.answer: The bigger triangle has rows 1 to n and the smaller has rows 1 to n−1; turned around, the smaller fits into the gap of the bigger, and every row becomes n long, making an n by n square
hints: Draw the triangles for 6 and 10.
Turn the 6-triangle upside down next to the 10-triangle.
Each row then has 4 dots, so the shape is ___ by ___.
Turned and fitted together, every row is n long, so they always make an n by n square.

verified.solverAnswer: two neighbouring triangles fit together as a square (staircase picture): T(n)+T(n-1)=n^2

items.prompt_en: Compare 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 and 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1. Which gives a triangular number and which gives a square?
items.prompt_hi: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 aur 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 ko compare karo. Kaunsa triangular number deta hai aur kaunsa square?
items.answer: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 is triangular; going up and back down gives 16, a square
hints: Work out both totals.
Going only up gives a triangle; up and back down gives something else.
10 is a triangular number; 16 is a square number (4 × 4).

items.prompt_en: A square rangoli has 5 rows of 5 dots. Meera extends it to 6 rows of 6 dots by adding dots along the bottom and right edges. How many dots does she add?
items.prompt_hi: Ek square rangoli mein 5 rows hain, har row mein 5 dots. Meera neeche aur daayein kinaare par dots jodkar use 6 rows aur 6 columns ka banati hai. Kitne dots judte hain?
items.answer: 11 dots
hints: Which dots belong to the new border?
Think of the border as the next odd-sized layer.
New dots = new square’s dots − old square’s dots = ___.
11 dots: the 6 × 6 square has 11 more than the 5 × 5 square.

items.prompt_en: For a school display, one triangular arrangement has 10 badges in 4 rows; the next has 15 badges in 5 rows. If the two arrangements fit together to form a square, how many badges are in that square?
items.prompt_hi: School display mein ek triangular arrangement ki 4 rows mein 10 badges hain; agle arrangement ki 5 rows mein 15 badges hain. Dono milkar square banate hain. Us square mein kitne badges hain?
items.answer: 25 badges
hints: What must you combine to count the square?
The two triangles are consecutive triangular numbers.
Badges in the square = badges in both triangles added = ___.
25 badges: the two arrangements together form a 5 × 5 square.

items.prompt_en: A stadium lights a square grid in stages: first 1 light, then 3 more, then 5 more, continuing through 29 more. How many lights are on? Use the pattern rather than adding every number.
items.prompt_hi: Stadium mein square grid ki lights stages mein jalti hain: pehle 1, phir 3 aur, phir 5 aur, aise hi 29 aur tak. Kul kitni lights jalengi? Sab numbers alag-alag jodne ke bajay pattern use karo.
items.answer: 225 lights
hints: Which stage ends with the given odd number?
Each new odd layer makes the square’s side one longer.
Number of odd layers = ___; square that number.
225 lights: there are 15 odd layers, making a 15 × 15 square.

items.prompt_en: At a kabaddi event, two consecutive triangular seating sections have 12 and 13 rows. They join to make a square seating block. How many seats are in the block?
items.prompt_hi: Kabaddi event mein do lagataar triangular seating sections ki 12 aur 13 rows hain. Dono judkar square seating block banate hain. Block mein kul kitni seats hain?
items.answer: 169 seats
hints: What is the side length of the joined square?
Consecutive triangles with these row counts complete a square.
Seats in the block = square of ___ rows.
169 seats: the sections join into a 13 × 13 square.

items.prompt_en: A phone game adds dots in L-shaped layers: 1, then 3, then 5, and so on. Which explains why every total is square: A) Each new L completes a larger square; B) Any sum of odd numbers is square?
items.prompt_hi: Phone game mein dots L-shape layers mein judte hain: pehle 1, phir 3, phir 5, aur aise hi. Har total square kyun hai? A) Har naya L bada square poora karta hai; B) Odd numbers ka koi bhi sum square hota hai?
items.answer: A — Each new L completes a larger square
acceptable: Each new L completes a larger square
Har naya L bada square poora karta hai
hints: How does the dot picture change after each move?
Focus on the shape made by all dots, not just their count.
Each added layer fills the border of a larger ___.
A: each new L completes a larger square, so every total is square.

workedExample.problem: Show that 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16 using a picture.
steps: Start with 1 dot in the corner.
Add 3 dots as an L around it: a 2 by 2 square, 4 dots.
Add 5 dots as the next L: a 3 by 3 square, 9 dots.
Add 7 dots as the next L: a 4 by 4 square, 16 dots.

Add 3 dots as an L around it: a 2 by 2 square, ___ dots.

Each odd number is one L-shape, so 4 odd numbers make a 4 by 4 square.

skills.title: Count sides and corners in the regular polygon sequence
Count lines joining every pair of points and small shapes in stacked figures
Link a shape pattern to a number sequence and predict the next count (including the Koch snowflake)

expectations: Regular polygons have equal sides and equal angles; their sides go 3, 4, 5, 6 … (the counting numbers from 3)

A big triangle made of small triangles with 1, 2, 3, 4 rows has 1, 4, 9, 16 small triangles: the square numbers

Shape patterns hide number sequences, so we can predict the next shape by its number rule

Says 'shapes are geometry, sequences are numbers'

items.prompt_en: A square and a rhombus both have 4 equal sides. Which is a regular polygon, and why?

items.answer: The square: a regular polygon needs equal sides AND equal angles; a rhombus that is not a square has unequal angles

items.prompt_en: Teach a friend how the joining-points pattern is connected to triangular numbers.

items.answer: 768 segments

Use the same multiplier twice after stage 3.
Stage 5 count = 48 × ___ × ___.
768 segments; multiplying 48 by 4 twice gives the stage 5 count.

items.prompt_en: A shopkeeper glances at a basket and says, '₹1000 will be enough.' Why is an estimate useful here, even though it is not exact?

items.prompt_en: A cricket club buys 25 jerseys at ₹398 each. Find the exact total mentally by using ₹400 per jersey, then adjusting.
items.prompt_hi: Cricket club 25 jerseys kharidta hai, har ek ₹398 ki. Pehle ₹400 per jersey lekar, phir adjust karke exact total mann mein nikalo.

nau hazaar nau sau pachaas rupaye

Ticks some items twice

options.text: The total is 32, not 30, so something was counted wrongly
Nothing, the table is fine
Cricket is the favourite, that's all

items.prompt_en: How many does this tally show: one bundle of five plus three single lines?

A bundle is five.

items.prompt_en: Favourite fruits: mango, apple, mango, banana, mango, apple, guava, mango, banana, mango. Make a frequency count.

items.answer: Mango 5, apple 2, banana 2, guava 1

Go through once, putting one tally mark per fruit.
Mango ___, apple 2, banana 2, guava 1; check the total is 10.
Mango 5, apple 2, banana 2, guava 1, total 10.

items.prompt_en: From that table (mango 5, apple 2, banana 2, guava 1), how many more children chose mango than apple?

hints: How many chose mango? Apple?
'How many more' means take away.
3 more.

items.prompt_en: Why is a frequency table easier than the list of 10 fruits for answering 'Which fruit is the favourite?'
items.prompt_hi: 'Favourite fruit kaunsa hai?' iska jawab dene ke liye 10 fruits ki list se frequency table aasaan kyon hai?
items.answer: The table has already grouped and counted each fruit, so you just pick the biggest number instead of re-counting the list

You would count each fruit again.
The table shows each fruit's ___ at once.
Because the counting is already done; the biggest frequency shows the favourite.

items.prompt_en: Before counting, predict: four tally bundles and two single lines make what number?
items.prompt_hi: Ginne se pehle guess karo: chaar tally bundles aur do akeli lines kaunsa number banate hain?
hints: How much is each bundle?
Four bundles of five, then the extra lines.

items.prompt_en: Neha says this tally shows 7: one full bundle (four upright lines with a fifth line drawn across them), plus three more lines. Check her.
items.prompt_hi: Neha kehti hai yeh tally 7 dikhati hai: ek poora bundle (chaar khadi lines aur unke upar paanchvi line aar-paar), aur teen aur lines. Check karo.
items.answer: It shows 8; the line across counts as the fifth mark
hints: How many marks are in the crossed bundle?
Four upright lines plus the line across = 5.
8: the crossing line is the fifth mark.

items.prompt_en: 30 children were surveyed. The table says cricket 12, football 9, kabaddi 7, badminton 4. Is there a problem?

items.answer: Yes: the frequencies add to 32, not 30, so something was counted wrongly
hints: Add all the frequencies.
Compare the total with the number of children.
Yes: 32 is not 30, so some answers were counted twice or wrongly.

items.prompt_en: How children in a colony get to school: walk 14, bus 9, auto-rickshaw 6, cycle 11. How many children altogether, and which way is least used?
items.prompt_hi: Ek colony ke bachche school kaise jaate hain: paidal 14, bus 9, auto-rickshaw 6, cycle 11. Kul kitne bachche hain, aur sabse kam kaunsa tareeka?
items.answer: 40 children; auto-rickshaw is least used
hints: Add the four numbers.
14 + 9 + 6 + 11; then find the smallest.
Total = ___, smallest = auto-rickshaw.
40 children; auto-rickshaw (6) is least.

items.prompt_en: Two survey questions: 'What is your favourite sport?' and 'Do you like sports?' Which gives more useful data for planning a sports day, and why?

items.answer: The first: it gives categories (cricket, kho-kho …) you can count to choose events; the second gives only yes or no

To choose events you need to know which sports.
The first gives ___ we can count.
The favourite-sport question, because it gives sport categories to count.

items.prompt_en: Your class wants to choose a picnic place. Plan the data: what question will you ask, what options, and how will you record the answers?

items.answer: Ask one clear question with fixed options (e.g. zoo, lake, fort), record one tally per child, count frequencies, check the total equals class size, and pick the highest
hints: What exact question would you ask?
Give a few fixed choices so answers can be counted.
Question → options → tally → frequencies → check total = ___.
One clear question with fixed options, tally each answer, count, check the total, choose the highest.

Then one tally mark per answer.

Four upright lines crossed by a fifth.

4 responses; the listed frequencies total 32, not 36.

items.prompt_en: Teach a friend how to draw a circle of radius 3 cm with a compass.

items.prompt_en: Meera wants to draw a circular design 12 cm across on a notebook cover. How wide should she set her compass?

items.prompt_en: For a poster, you need a short arc from a circle 10 cm across. With the compass point fixed at O, what opening should you use before drawing the arc?

items.prompt_en: A metro map marks stations A and B exactly 4 km from hub H. A planner draws a circle centred at H with radius 4 km. Will both stations lie on the circle? Answer yes or no.

items.answer: yes

items.prompt_en: How many right angles does a rectangle have?

Every corner is a right angle.
A rectangle has ___ right angles.

items.prompt_en: A rectangle has one side 7 cm and the next side 4 cm. What are the other two sides?

items.answer: 7 cm and 4 cm

Opposite sides are equal.

items.prompt_en: Push a square frame made of four equal sticks so it leans. Predict: is it still a square?

items.answer: No: the sides stay equal but the angles are no longer 90°, so it is a rhombus

Two corners get narrow and two get wide.

No: it becomes a rhombus.

items.prompt_en: Why do we need to check angles, not just sides, when constructing a square?

items.answer: Equal sides alone allow a squashed shape (a rhombus); a square also needs four right angles
hints: Can four equal sides make a shape that is not a square?
A leaning frame has equal sides.
A square needs equal sides AND ___ angles.
Because four equal sides can still lean into a rhombus; the right angles make it a square.

verified.solverAnswer: equal sides alone could be a slanted rhombus; need right angles

items.prompt_en: Is every square a rectangle? Is every rectangle a square?
items.prompt_hi: Kya har square ek rectangle hai? Kya har rectangle ek square hai?
items.answer: Every square is a rectangle (four right angles, opposite sides equal); not every rectangle is a square
hints: List what a rectangle needs.
Four right angles and opposite sides equal: does a square have these?
Square → rectangle: ___; rectangle → square: only if all sides are equal.
Every square is a rectangle; a rectangle is a square only when all sides are equal.

verified.solverAnswer: every square is a rectangle; not every rectangle is a square

items.prompt_en: Neha says a square turned to stand on its corner becomes a diamond, not a square. Check her.

items.answer: It is still a square: turning changes neither the sides nor the angles

Did any angle change?
Same sides, same angles → still a ___.
Still a square: only its position changed.

items.prompt_en: Say the steps to construct a rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm.

AB = 6 cm, right angles at A and B, 4 cm up each to D and C, join DC.

items.prompt_en: You are constructing a square of side 5 cm. After drawing AB = 5 cm and right angles at A and B, how do you find C and D?
items.prompt_hi: Tum 5 cm side ka square bana rahe ho. AB = 5 cm aur A, B pe right angles banane ke baad C aur D kaise milenge?
items.answer: With the compass opened to 5 cm, mark 5 cm up each perpendicular from A and B, then join the two marks
hints: How long must AD and BC be?
All sides are 5 cm.
Open the compass to ___ cm and mark on both lines.
Mark 5 cm up each line with the compass and join D to C.

verified.solverAnswer: mark 5 cm up on each perpendicular, join

items.prompt_en: A carpenter makes a window frame with sides 60, 40, 60 and 40 cm, but it wobbles out of shape. What should he check to be sure it is a rectangle?
items.prompt_hi: Ek carpenter 60, 40, 60 aur 40 cm sides wala khidki ka frame banata hai, par woh tedha ho jaata hai. Rectangle pakka karne ke liye use kya check karna chahiye?
items.answer: That the corners are right angles (for example by checking the two diagonals are equal)
hints: Opposite sides are already equal. What else does a rectangle need?
Four right angles.
Check each corner is ___° (or the diagonals are equal).
The corners must be right angles; equal diagonals are a quick check.

items.prompt_en: Describe a rectangle using only its properties, without drawing it.

items.answer: A four-sided shape with four right angles whose opposite sides are equal

items.prompt_en: Teach a friend how to construct a square of side 4 cm.

Mark ___ cm with the compass, join, and check.
Draw 4 cm, make right angles at both ends, mark 4 cm with the compass, join, and check.

verified.solverAnswer: AB=4, right angles, 4 cm up, join

items.prompt_en: Quick! What does a square have that not every rectangle has?
